title: Folly
note: He turns from friendship to enmity, which springs from anger and desire. Their root is delusion, treated in two chapters, and the first is folly: knowing nothing at all.

couplets.plain: What is folly? It is taking hold of what harms you and letting go of what profits you.
couplets.pm: Folly is the worst of all the faults a person can have. It is taking up what brings ruin and letting go of what brings gain. Ruin here means poverty, blame and sin. Gain means wealth, fame and righteousness. So the fool wrecks this life and the next by his own hand.

links.quote: taking hold of what harms you and letting go of what profits you

couplets.plain: The worst folly of all is setting your heart on conduct that isn’t for you.
couplets.pm: The worst of all follies is to be fond of conduct that does you no good. He means gladly doing what the learned have forbidden as harmful in this life and the next.

links.reason: Ranks setting your heart on conduct that isn’t for you as the worst folly there is.

couplets.plain: Having no shame, looking into nothing, showing no warmth, caring for nothing: these are a fool’s habits.
couplets.pm: The fool feels no shame at blame and sin, does not look into which tasks to do and which to avoid, is harsh in word and deed with everyone, and guards nothing worth guarding, such as family, learning and conduct. They are called his “work” because they come to him naturally, at all times.

links.reason: Lists the fool’s habits: no shame, no inquiry, no warmth, no care for anything.

couplets.plain: No one is a greater fool than someone who studies, understands, teaches others, and still has no self-control.
couplets.pm: Someone studies the books that lead to control of mind, speech and body, understands what that control brings, and explains it to others who want to know, yet does not live by it. There is no greater fool in the world. The very things that cure folly have failed, and there is no other medicine.

links.quote: No one is a greater fool
links.reason: Study and teaching don’t save someone without self-control from being the worst fool of all.
Self-control is the one thing all that learning lacks, and the lack makes a fool.

couplets.plain: In a single birth, a fool can do enough to sink into the mire of hell for all seven births.
couplets.pm: Within this one birth a fool can bring about the hell he will sink into through all the births to come. All births fall under seven, so “seven” means all. Even in his earthly births his cruel deeds keep him in that hell’s pain. Few others could do so quickly the deeds that earn suffering without end.

links.quote: the mire of hell for all seven births

links.remove: Seed and sowing aren’t in the Tamil. The image came from the old English.

couplets.plain: When a fool who doesn’t know how takes on a task, the task falls apart and the fool ends up in fetters.
couplets.pm: When a fool who doesn’t know the right way to do a thing takes on a task, it rots from within past repair, and he himself is put in fetters. He ruins it and ruins himself. This is how a fool tries to make wealth.

links.quote: the fool ends up in fetters
links.reason: A fool who takes on a task without knowing how wrecks it and lands in fetters.

couplets.plain: When a fool comes into great wealth, strangers eat their fill and the fool’s own people go hungry.
couplets.pm: When a fool comes by great wealth through god and not his own effort, people with no tie to him are filled, while his own people, tied to him in every way, go hungry. “Great wealth” could have bought every good thing. Outsiders get all they want, and his own do not get even food.

links.quote: strangers eat their fill and the fool’s own people go hungry
links.reason: A fool’s wealth feeds outsiders and leaves his own people hungry.

couplets.plain: When a fool gets something of their own in hand, it is like a madman getting drunk.
couplets.pm: When a fool gets something into his hands as his own, he is like a man already mad who drinks liquor on top of his madness. “Gets” shows it came through god and not by his own effort. With folly and the giddiness of wealth together, his acts stagger like those of someone both mad and drunk.

couplets.plain: The friendship of fools is very sweet. When it ends, it brings no pain at all.
couplets.pm: When fools’ friendship with each other reaches parting, it gives neither of them any pain, and so it is very sweet. It wears away day by day, so the end doesn’t hurt. This is blame that sounds like praise.

links.quote: When it ends, it brings no pain at all

couplets.plain: A fool walking into a gathering of the worthy is like putting an unwashed foot on a bed.
couplets.pm: A fool entering an assembly of the worthy is like setting a foot that has trodden filth on a bed made for pleasure. “Unwashed” is a polite way of saying it. As the foot degrades the bed, the fool degrades the assembly.

links.quote: an unwashed foot on a bed
links.reason: A fool among the worthy soils the gathering as an unwashed foot soils a bed.
